objectives: State ordering guarantees at partition and application boundaries.
Handle ownership changes without advancing past unfinished work.
Plan retention, replay, and schema evolution together.
retrieval: L101: what does a committed checkpoint mean?
L027: what happens when a caller loses a response?

sections.title: Ordered delivery can still produce unordered effects
sections.markdown:
A partition delivers account updates version7 then8. The consumer starts two asynchronous calls. Version8 finishes first and version7 overwrites it later. The broker preserved append order; the application did not preserve the required effect order. Decide whether the operation needs ordered application, version-conditional writes, or a commutative aggregation before increasing concurrency.

A key is a statement about related work. Keying by account keeps an account's records together under a stable partitioning scheme; keying every event with a random ID spreads load but abandons that locality. More partitions are not a free change when routing existing entities and checkpoints must remain coherent.

sections.title: A rebalance is a transfer of responsibility
sections.markdown:
When membership changes, partition ownership can move between group members. A previous owner may still have work running after its assignment is revoked. Stop admitting new work for revoked partitions, drain or cancel bounded in-flight work, and commit only completed contiguous positions under the client protocol. A new owner can replay records whose completion was not durably checkpointed.

If offsets20,21,22 are in flight and only20 and22 finish, committing23 skips21 after a crash. The safe completed prefix ends after20; checkpoint21 while recording enough application identity to tolerate replay of22. Alternatively process one record at a time per partition if the workload permits the simpler invariant.

Group membership does not automatically fence arbitrary external effects. A slow old worker might reach an external sink after a new owner begins. Use a sink-side version check, operation identity, or an ownership epoch enforced by the destination where required. A timeout in the consumer is not proof that an outstanding write cannot arrive.

sections.title: Replay old events into a new reader
sections.markdown:
A reader originally accepted {amount:12} meaning whole units. A writer changes amount to mean minor units while preserving the same field name and numeric shape. Schema parsing succeeds and business meaning fails. Define a new field or explicit version and an unambiguous conversion rule. Test a new reader against retained old records, not just new writer output.

Our teaching pipeline supports v1 amount and v2 amount_minor_units with integer minor-unit semantics explicitly specified by the project. The version chooses the decoder; an unknown version is rejected rather than guessed as zero. Store an event ID, entity ID, event type/version, and relevant time with the payload. An envelope is not permission to include secrets or arbitrary sensitive fields.

Illustrative recovery calculation: the group consumes5,000/s while new records arrive4,000/s. It can drain a backlog of3.6million in3,600 seconds if these rates remain stable: backlog /(service−arrival). A6-hour retention window leaves little safety if outages, rebalances, and retries consume the rest. Track oldest remaining age as well as count.

sections.title: Compatibility is a test matrix
sections.markdown:
Backward and forward compatibility refer to directions between writers and readers under a specific encoding's rules. A field default can let a decoder read an old payload but cannot manufacture a missing business fact. Enum additions, removed fields, renamed meanings, and unit changes deserve explicit examples. Keep versioned fixtures and run both replay and live-path tests.

Replaying into a separate named projection allows comparison before switching readers. Rate-limit recovery so it does not starve live processing or overwhelm a downstream database. Side effects such as notifications should not be reissued simply because a projection rebuild rereads history; isolate deterministic transformation from external commands.

Common mistakes: checkpointing the largest completed offset rather than the contiguous prefix; treating a rebalance as a clean process stop; assuming a syntactically compatible schema preserves meaning; and making retention shorter than the supported recovery interval. Optional exercise: draft a partition-count migration with a versioned routing epoch and per-entity barrier. That migration is outside the core ten-minute task.

diagrams.caption: The checkpoint represents the next record to process. Completion out of order requires tracking the contiguous prefix.
steps: Finish20 and advance next position to21.
Allow22 to finish without pretending21 is complete.
Recover and replay from21 after a crash.
Make repeated22 safe at its destination.

exercise.prompt: Offsets50–53 were fetched;50,52,53 completed but51 timed out. The owner is revoked. State the safe checkpoint, what the new owner may repeat, and how a versioned projection prevents stale overwrites. Then propose a compatibility test for changing money from units to minor units.
rubric: Test semantic meaning with retained fixtures.
exercise.solution: Checkpoint51, the next position after completed50. The new owner can replay51–53, including effects52/53 that already happened. A conditional version update rejects older entity versions, while durable event IDs prevent applying the same increment twice. Query/reconcile51 if its destination outcome is uncertain. Introduce explicit unit/version semantics and run old and new fixture events through the new decoder, comparing known totals; merely checking JSON parsing is insufficient.

questions.prompt: Completed offsets10 and12 with11 unfinished permit which next-position checkpoint?
questions.explanation: The prefix ends at10; advancing beyond11 loses its processing on restart.

questions.prompt: Partition append order guarantees external async writes finish in order?
questions.explanation: Application concurrency and destination behavior can reorder effects.

questions.answer: It preserves the live view while permitting full reconciliation, rollback, and a measured cutover instead of rebuilding live state in place.
